Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, between Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, independent since 1991. Its capital is Minsk. "Byelarus" and "Byelorussia" are older spellings, and "White Russia" is the literal English meaning.

For centuries its lands belonged to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and then Poland-Lithuania, before Russia took them in the late 18th century. As the Byelorussian Soviet republic it suffered terribly in the Second World War, losing a large share of its people. In 1986 much of the fallout from the Chernobyl disaster landed on its south.

It declared independence in 1991, and its leaders signed the Belavezha Accords that ended the Soviet Union, near Brest that December. Since 1994 Alexander Lukashenko has ruled, keeping much of the Soviet-style economy and binding the country closely to Russia. Mass protests after the disputed election of 2020 were crushed. In 2022 Russian troops used Belarus as a base when Russia invaded Ukraine.
